claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has moderate hardness and compressive strength.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has a low or minimal level of short-range order.
Low short-range order provides few obstacles to dislocation motion.
Relatively unobstructed dislocation motion causes the alloy's favorable plasticity and machinability.
Insufficient dislocation pinning causes the alloy's relatively low hardness and compressive strength.
Short-range order or secondary-phase precipitation can provide additional dislocation pinning and strengthening.
Heat treatment at approximately 400–500 °C can increase short-range order in CoCrFeNiTi without causing secondary-phase precipitation.
Increasing short-range order raises barriers to dislocation motion.
Increasing short-range order will increase the hardness of single-phase CoCrFeNiTi.
Increasing short-range order will increase the compressive strength of single-phase CoCrFeNiTi.
The predicted strengthening and hardening should be observable at both 25 °C and 600 °C.
Increasing short-range order is expected to reduce ductility or plasticity while increasing strength.
The proposed mechanism is limited to equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi that remains free of secondary precipitation.
The proposed mechanism is limited to testing from 25 °C through 600 °C at moderate strain rates.

contradictions.description: The comparator is alternately called 'as-cast' and 'as-cast, homogenized.' Homogenization is a post-casting treatment, so the actual baseline state is terminologically ambiguous.
Reduced ductility is presented as only a possible outcome ('may occur') in the prediction, but its absence during successful strengthening is treated as falsifying the hypothesis.
